mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 shows a sustained decline for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending drives economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS show simultaneous increases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls indicates a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as wage pressures and consumer spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases & PAYEMS increases in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases and PAYEMS increases in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the Federal Reserve is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL shows a sustained increase for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail sales coupled with a rise in unemployment rate signals a weakening consumer demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases & UNRATE increases in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS decreases and UNRATE increases in a month.
